info.title: TenkaCloud Simulator API
info.description:
Sign in through the local console first. The browser sends its same-origin session cookie; Test Request uses that session. For curl or SDKs add the host-issued `X-Simulator-Token` header. Dummy TCSIM signature credentials identify the AWS wire format; they are not host authentication. `x-simulator-principal` selects an exercise identity only. Participant sessions are already bound to an identity and cannot select simulator-admin. Never enter real AWS credentials here. 

**Examples are static documentation, not saved state.** Use Test Request → Send to query your environment. S3 responses remain native XML/bytes; expand typed schemas below to understand fields.

Independent local cloud simulator. AWS is the first provider, with documented S3, Systems Manager Parameter Store, SQS, Lambda, CloudFormation and IAM role subsets. No real infrastructure is created. This document describes only implemented operations. S3 wire APIs retain their XML formats; Native IAM roles use Query/XML; legacy identity control remains a separate JSON API. Native role ownership blocks legacy PUT/DELETE with HTTP409. Use unsigned requests or dummy TCSIM SDK credentials. Default principal simulator-admin has full sandbox access. IAM Query routing uses X-Simulator-Service: iam (or the dummy SDK signature scope), root POST and Version2010-05-08. Nine bounded role/inline-policy operations are implemented; no STS, managed policies, Conditions or non-root paths. Native Lambda roles must trust lambda.amazonaws.com. Legacy CFN/local identity roles retain their prior metadata-only trust semantics. For IAM exercises send x-simulator-principal. SQLite is ephemeral by default; --state persists it. See /_simulator/v1/capabilities for limits and deviations. Lambda supports a bounded Python 3.12 ZIP subset through the native REST paths below. Host Python is not required. A limited saved-role local SSM/S3 function SDK is supported; arbitrary network/HTTP and Function URLs remain unsupported. CloudFormation supports inline Python AWS::Lambda::Function with index.handler, existing local role, Ref/Arn and explicit DependsOn. Caller requires Lambda Create/DeleteFunction and iam:PassRole; tagged creation also requires lambda:TagResource. Only the declared saved-role SSM/S3 capability bridge is available, with no arbitrary network or managed-policy grants. Function SDK limits: S3 object body32KiB, native response48KiB before capability encoding, message64KiB,128calls and1MiB request/response aggregate. Oversized native SSM or S3 responses return EntityTooLarge without a partial successful result. API Gateway REST APIs support an explicit REGIONAL/NONE/Lambda AWS_PROXY subset. Deployments freeze resources and integrations; stages refer to a deployment. No public endpoint or real AWS is created. Local invocation requires the host access token/session and a bounded Lambda apigateway.amazonaws.com resource permission with a matching local execute-api SourceArn. Responses are non-executing downloads, with protected cookie/navigation/CORS/CSP headers removed. Active browser app hosting, WAF, custom domains, authorizers, binary media, API keys, caching, stage editing and full WP grading remain unsupported. CloudFormation also provisions the bounded RestApi/Resource/Method/Deployment/Stage and Lambda::Permission subset in the same native SQLite transaction. Deployment DependsOn methods is explicit; API children are same-stack, snapshots immutable, and native drift blocks destructive cleanup. No WAF or custom resources are supported.

Google Cloud Storage JSON API and Azure Blob Storage REST are bounded independently implemented local providers. Synthetic project/account scope and owner bindings are host configured; Google IAM/Azure RBAC, cloud account provisioning, OAuth/Entra/SharedKey/SAS are not implemented. See the provider-specific operations below and capabilities; SDK compatibility is separately tested and must not be inferred from API existence. DynamoDB supports seven basic JSON 1.0 operations at the shared regional root and a bounded table/item console; Query/Scan, indexes and CFN remain unsupported.

get.description:
**Static examples below are sample documentation, not your current state.** Click **Test Request**, then **Send** to execute this operation. The client shows the live HTTP status, headers and body. Lists the buckets currently saved in this environment, across the supported regions. `Buckets/Bucket/Name` is a bucket name; `BucketRegion` is its saved region; `CreationDate` is UTC. An actually executed response with `<Buckets></Buckets>` is empty. The example below intentionally contains two sample buckets. Requires `s3:ListAllMyBuckets` on `*`.

**Local access:** browser requests use your signed-in simulator session. curl/SDK clients need the host-issued X-Simulator-Token. Dummy AWS signature keys are not login credentials. A host 401 means sign in again; an IAM 403 means the current exercise identity lacks permission.

After a live S3 metadata request, use the **Live S3 result · Read fields** button or **Alt+Shift+R** for a bounded field explanation. The API client keeps the original XML. The explanation is not available for arbitrary object bodies.

post.description:
**Static request templates:** choose the correct Content-Type and routing headers before Test Request → Send. SSM/SQS send JSON with X-Amz-Target (JSON 1.1 for SSM, JSON 1.0 for SQS); CloudFormation/IAM send URL-encoded Query fields. The 200 response is JSON for SSM/SQS and XML for Query protocols. A successful DeleteStack has no result payload beyond Query response metadata.

Native regional root endpoint. SQS: X-Amz-Target AmazonSQS.CreateQueue, ListQueues, GetQueueUrl, DeleteQueue, SendMessage, ReceiveMessage, DeleteMessage, ChangeMessageVisibility, GetQueueAttributes (JSON 1.0, Standard queues only; local body limit 256 KiB, aggregate physical storage 10000 messages/64 MiB across queues/regions including expired foreign rows until scoped cleanup; bytes count body UTF-8 plus stored attribute JSON. Over-budget SendMessage returns local SimulatorQuotaExceeded without mutation; existing over-cap data remains readable/deletable; FIFO, Query protocol, batch operations and dead-letter redrive are unsupported). SSM: X-Amz-Target AmazonSSM.PutParameter, GetParameter, GetParameters, GetParametersByPath, DescribeParameters, DeleteParameter. CloudFormation: CreateStack, DescribeStacks, DeleteStack; S3 buckets, SSM parameters, inline Python Lambda functions, one inline IAM identity policy per role, five Regional REST API Gateway resource types, and bounded Lambda::Permission. Unsupported options fail. Real credentials and session tokens are rejected. Create/DeleteStack also require the caller to allow the underlying S3/SSM/IAM/Lambda actions; CAPABILITY_IAM grants no permissions. API resources use NONE/POST AWS_PROXY local Lambda, same-stack API children, explicit deployment DependsOn methods and reverse guarded cleanup. Lambda permission uses only apigateway.amazonaws.com and local execute-api SourceArn. No service RoleArn or general CloudFormation lifecycle is supported. IAM customer-managed policies and role attachments are also available through the dedicated IAM provider template, with explicit ListPolicies Scope=Local. IAM is global: send X-Simulator-Service: iam, Version2010-05-08 and one of CreateRole/GetRole/ListRoles/DeleteRole/PutRolePolicy/GetRolePolicy/DeleteRolePolicy/ListRolePolicies/UpdateAssumeRolePolicy. Policy documents are JSON strings; successful IAM XML returns them RFC3986 URL-encoded. Native role names use the local alphanumeric/underscore/hyphen subset,1–64; inline policy names1–128 AWS characters. Trust and aggregate policies32KiB, at most10 inline policies/100 statements,1000 active+retired name claims. Deleted role names cannot be adopted by legacy identity writes. No managed grants or session issuance.

**Local access:** browser requests use your signed-in simulator session. curl/SDK clients need the host-issued X-Simulator-Token. Dummy AWS signature keys are not login credentials. A host 401 means sign in again; an IAM 403 means the current exercise identity lacks permission.

Use X-Amz-Target TrentService.<operation> matching the selected body example; example choice does not change routing headers automatically. CreateKey first, copy returned KeyId into later requests, and copy an actual local Encrypt CiphertextBlob into Decrypt (the valid-base64 documentation placeholder is deliberately not decryptable). All calls require host X-Simulator-Token or signed-in local session. Dummy TCSIM SigV4 scope is not authentication.

CreateKey/ListKeys require their exact kms action on *. DescribeKey/EnableKey/DisableKey/GetKeyPolicy/Encrypt/Decrypt require the actual key ARN. Decrypt without KeyId resolves the local blob key. Explicit Deny wins. Programmatic default policy only enables local identity-policy delegation; no grant for all participants.

Enabled/Disabled only; disabled blocks Encrypt/Decrypt, metadata/default policy remain readable. Local request64KiB,1000keys,plaintext1–4096bytes,context100entries/8192canonicalbytes,counter2^32 ceiling. Ciphertext/material are simulator-local; SQLite stores raw material, not an at-rest security boundary. Unsupported aliases/tags/grants/custom policies/asymmetric/data keys/rotation/deletion/multi-region/CFN/other-service encryption fail; no problem availability is implied. Actual AWS eventual consistency and ciphertext portability are not reproduced.

KMS JSON1.1 targets TrentService.CreateKey/DescribeKey/ListKeys/EnableKey/DisableKey/GetKeyPolicy/Encrypt/Decrypt are also accepted here. This root JSON1.1 section includes all eight bounded KMS body templates and limitations.

SQS static templates use application/x-amz-json-1.0 with X-Amz-Target: AmazonSQS.<operation> and X-Simulator-Service: sqs. Replace QueueUrl and ReceiptHandle fixtures with current native values; static examples are not live saved state. CloudWatch Logs JSON1.1 uses Logs_20140328.<operation> and service=logs; only the seven declared operations are implemented. Choose the matching headers separately from the body example. Secrets Manager adds seven bounded JSON1.1 operations over this same root; practice values are plaintext, not KMS-encrypted. No recovery window or rotation.

**DynamoDB JSON 1.0 static templates:** select application/x-amz-json-1.0 and set X-Amz-Target to the exact DynamoDB_20120810.<operation> shown by the selected example. X-Simulator-Service may be dynamodb. Use a private practice table name; samples are not current state and selecting a body does not automatically change the target header. Seven basic operations only; immediate local lifecycle, no indexes/Query/Scan/console/CFN. DeleteItem of an absent key is idempotent; unsupported options fail. Item bytes use UTF-8 and decoded binary rather than JSON transfer length; numeric sizing is approximate. Failed conditional, oversized and IAM-refused writes leave saved state unchanged. DeleteTable permanently removes that practice table and all its items.

KMS aliases: TrentService.CreateAlias, ListAliases, UpdateAlias, DeleteAlias. Customer alias names include alias/ and are case-sensitive; alias/aws/ is reserved. Alias targets are concrete local key IDs/ARNs in the same account/Region. Create requires kms:CreateAlias on alias+target, Update kms:UpdateAlias on alias+old+new, Delete kms:DeleteAlias on alias+target, List kms:ListAliases on *. Local aliases are capped at1000 total/50 per key; ListAliases defaults50 and accepts1–100. Create/Update/Delete return empty200. Encrypt/Decrypt accept aliases, resolving and authorizing the concrete key in the same transaction. No alias identifiers for DescribeKey/EnableKey/DisableKey/GetKeyPolicy, AWS-managed aliases, alias ABAC, key deletion lifecycle, grants or CFN KMS resources.

put.description:
**Static examples below are sample documentation, not your current state.** Click **Test Request**, then **Send** to execute this operation. The client shows the live HTTP status, headers and body. Requires s3:CreateBucket on the bucket ARN. Empty body creates in us-east-1. Other supported regions require LocationConstraint. Bucket subresources: use ?versioning for Get/PutBucketVersioning; ?publicAccessBlock for Get/Put/DeletePublicAccessBlock; ?versions for GET ListObjectVersions. Do not combine subresources or send list-type with them. Versioning Status is Enabled/Suspended; MFA Delete is unsupported. Public access block stores the four bucket-level booleans; public ACLs/policies remain unsupported. Bucket tags use ?tagging. GET requires s3:GetBucketTagging; PUT/DELETE require s3:PutBucketTagging. User-defined metadata only, no ABAC/billing/system tags. An empty replacement removes the set; an absent set returns NoSuchTagSet.

**Local access:** browser requests use your signed-in simulator session. curl/SDK clients need the host-issued X-Simulator-Token. Dummy AWS signature keys are not login credentials. A host 401 means sign in again; an IAM 403 means the current exercise identity lacks permission.
